# Fairstay 13 Week Cash Flow (`fairstay-13-week-cash-flow`)

13-week cash projection for a nursing home from opening cash, receivables and collection rates by payer type, new billing with its lag, payroll dates, bills due and fixed monthly payments, flagging weeks below your minimum cash or overdrawn. Arithmetic on your numbers, not a forecast. Bank account numbers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay 13 Week Cash Flow never draws on a credit line or moves money.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-13-week-cash-flow demo
npx -y fairstay-13-week-cash-flow mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

A fictional Cedar Hollow 13-week projection starting Monday 6 April 2026. Planted:

- A pharmacy bill due 2 April is already past due, so it lands in week 1.
- Week 1 has payroll, insurance and that bill together, so cash dips 8510 below the 250000 minimum.
- Hospice receivables have no collection rate in the plan, so they are left out and listed.
- The provider tax in week 6 and rent on the 1st of each month are spread through the weeks.

Bank account numbers are listed in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`plan-typo.json`](fixtures/plan-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the projection refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `cashflow_check` | Build the week-by-week projection and list weeks below the minimum. | runs |
| `cashflow_write_report` | Write cashflow-cash-13-week.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and cashflow-cash-13-week.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/cashflow). | runs |
| `cashflow_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `cashflow_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `cashflow_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `cashflow_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `line_draw` | Fairstay 13 Week Cash Flow never draws on a credit line or moves money. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `cashflow_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `opening` (required) | Cash balances today under --root: account, balance |
| `ar` (required) | Open receivables under --root: payer or payer type, amount (an aging summary is enough) |
| `bills` | Bills to pay under --root: vendor, due date, amount |
| `plan` (required) | Plan JSON: collection rates, weekly billing and lag by payer type, payroll, fixed payments, minimum cash |
| `start` | First day of week 1 (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-13-week-cash-flow inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Cash balances (`opening`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `account` | text (masked) | Account, Account Number, Bank Account, Acct |
| `balance` (required) | amount | Balance, Ending Balance, Available, Ledger Balance, Amount |

### Receivables (`ar`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Balance, Open Balance, Total |

### Bills due (`bills`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` | text | Vendor, Payee, Vendor Name |
| `due_date` (required) | date | Due Date, Due, Pay Date |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |

## Settings file (`cashflow_plan`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `collect` | How today's receivables come in, by payer type |
| `weekly_billing` | New revenue billed each week, by payer type |
| `lag` | When new billing turns into cash, by payer type |
| `payroll` | Payroll |
| `fixed` | Fixed monthly payments |
| `min_cash` | Lowest cash you are comfortable with |

## Memory

`cashflow_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `cashflow_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `cash_note` | is shown with results. It never changes the projection. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-13-week-cash-flow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-13-week-cash-flow",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-13-week-cash-flow -- npx -y fairstay-13-week-cash-flow mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-13-week-cash-flow tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-13-week-cash-flow sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-13-week-cash-flow inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-13-week-cash-flow call cashflow_check '{"opening":"<opening>","ar":"<ar>","plan":"<plan>"}'
fairstay-13-week-cash-flow eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-13-week-cash-flow demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
